hydration.note: The National Academies set the Adequate Intake for total water at 3.7 L/day for men aged 19–30, with about 3.0 L (13 cups) coming from drinks and the rest from food. It is an intake level, not a minimum you must hit — thirst is a good guide for most healthy people, and heat or heavy sweating raises the need.
cues: Front-load: 1 L before noon while you are fasting anyway.
Pale straw urine is the practical check. Dark yellow means catch up.
Add 500 ml for every sweaty training session.
Count tea and coffee — they contribute to fluid intake.

sleep.note: The AASM and Sleep Research Society consensus is 7 or more hours a night for adults; 6 or fewer is not enough to sustain health. There is no upper limit in the recommendation.

routine.why: CDC advises no caffeine within 5 hours of bed, more if you are sensitive. This leaves a wide margin.
Large meals close to bed disrupt sleep, and it is the same clock that anchors your 16:8 window.

routine.do: Caffeine-free herbal tea, lights down, screens off if you can
routine.why: A consistent wind-down cue matters more than any single tactic.

routine.do: Lights out — same time every night, weekends included
routine.why: CDC puts a consistent schedule first among sleep habits, because it is what actually regulates the body clock.

routine.do: Same wake time, daylight within 30 minutes
routine.why: A fixed wake time is the anchor that makes the fixed bedtime possible.

environment: Dark: blackout curtains or an eye mask.
Cool and quiet; earplugs or a fan if the street is loud.
No alcohol before bed — it fragments the second half of the night.
If you are awake more than 20 minutes, get up and do something dull in dim light rather than lying there.

habits.label: No sugar-sweetened drinks, no ultra-processed snacks

longevity.framework: The eight things the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 identifies as the drivers of cardiovascular health — which is also the best-evidenced proxy we have for healthspan. Each one is scored here against its own published target rather than AHA's 0–100 point algorithm.

components.label: Diet
components.target: Follow the Dietary Guidelines pattern: 3 vegetable servings, 2 fruit, 2–4 whole grains, 3 dairy, 1.2–1.6 g/kg protein, minimal ultra-processed food

components.label: Physical activity
components.target: 150–300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus 2+ strength days

components.label: Nicotine exposure
components.target: None — including vaping and second-hand smoke

components.label: Blood lipids
components.target: Total cholesterol under 200 mg/dL, LDL under 100, HDL 40 or above, triglycerides under 150

components.label: Blood glucose
components.target: Fasting glucose under 100 mg/dL; A1c under 5.7%

biomarkers.label: Waist circumference
biomarkers.target: Under 40 in for men — above that raises risk of type 2 diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular disease even at a normal weight

biomarkers.label: Resting heart rate
biomarkers.target: Watch the trend; a falling resting rate over months means the aerobic work is landing

biomarkers.label: Steps
biomarkers.target: No official guideline sets a step count — this is a personal proxy for the guideline's 150–300 weekly minutes

biomarkers.label: VO2 max (from a watch or lab test)
biomarkers.target: Above 28 for men — below that is the low-fitness band in AHA's scientific statement

screening.when: At least yearly, and any time you can get it checked free
screening.why: USPSTF recommends screening every adult 18 and over. High blood pressure has no symptoms.

screening.what: Prediabetes and type 2 diabetes (fasting glucose or A1c)
screening.why: USPSTF recommends screening adults aged 35–70 who carry overweight or obesity. You are under 35 but already above the BMI 25 threshold, which is worth raising with a clinician rather than waiting three years.

screening.when: Ask at your next appointment, then on your clinician's schedule
screening.why: Gives you the LDL, HDL and triglyceride baseline this app tracks against, and it is the one longevity input you cannot estimate at home.
Cheap, and gum disease tracks with cardiovascular risk.
Also the earliest place raised blood pressure and blood sugar show up as visible damage.

milestones.note: NHLBI's advice for adults carrying overweight is to aim for 5–10% of starting weight over about six months. At 182.5 lb that is the first two milestones below. The BMI-based targets come after.

steps.label: 5% down — the first clinically meaningful step
10% down — most of the metabolic benefit shows up here
BMI 27 — halfway out of the overweight band
BMI 23 — comfortably inside it, with room for muscle gain

principles: Weight comes off at 1–2 lb a week or it comes back. CDC is blunt about this: gradual and steady is what stays off.
The fasting window controls when you eat. It does not decide what you eat — that is what the food-group targets are for.
Protein and fibre are the two levers that make a calorie deficit tolerable. Every meal in this plan carries both.
Strength training is the part that protects you at 60, not the part that changes the scale at 33. Do not drop it when the weight stalls.
A stall of two or three weeks is normal. A stall of six weeks means the intake estimate needs revisiting, not that the plan failed.
